originalTitle: Michael Cohen, ex-fixer for Trump who once testified against him, hosts president on his radio show – US politics live
summary: Despite previously comparing him to a ‘mobster’, Trump’s former personal lawyer showers him with praise
content: Donald Trump’s former fixer and personal lawyer, Michael Cohen, who turned on the president in 2019, when he compared him to a mobster during congressional testimony, executed another 180-degree turn on Thursday, when showered the president with praise during a friendly conversation between the two men broadcast on Cohen’s New York City radio show. Cohen, who played the 1970s R&B hit Reunited in the background as he told listeners to tune in on Sunday for more of the interview, introduced the chat by saying that the two men had forgiven each other. Cohen then criticized people who think “holding on to hatred is a sign of strength”. Trump, famously, holds grudges for decades. In the part of the conversation broadcast on Thursday, Cohen fully supported Trump’s baseless claim that Iran would have obtained nuclear weapons and destroyed Israel by now had he not been elected president in 2024. That claim is contradicted by the fact that a 2025 US intelligence assessment, released shortly before Trump ordered strikes on Iran’s nuclear enrichment facilities, said that Iran had abandoned its pursuit of nuclear weapons in 2003. In the chat, Cohen also tried to job Trump’s memory of his former role as his closest aide by saying, “Boss, you remember when I was by your side?” At another stage in the conversation, Trump appeared to tacitly admit that he actually lost the 2020 presidential election when he told Cohen: “I got elected on the border - by the way that happened two times” and then referring to the 2016 and 2024 elections. Trump went on to claim that Cohen had been unfairly threatened with jail by the Manhattan and New York state prosecutors who used his testimony to convict Trump of campaign finance violations and fraud. In 2018, Cohen pleaded guilty in federal court to orchestrating $280,000 in payments during Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign to buy the silence of two women who threatened to speak publicly about their alleged affairs with Trump. In 2019, after defecting from Trump’s orbit, Cohen told Congress: “I am ashamed that I chose to take part in concealing Mr. Trump’s illicit acts rather than listening to my own conscience. I am ashamed, because I know what Mr. Trump is. He is a racist, he is a con man, and he is a cheat.” In the same testimony, Cohen provided a Democratic-led committee with what he said was a copy of a check Trump wrote from his personal bank account to reimburse Cohen for hush-money payments to one of the women, Stormy Daniels, “to cover up his affair with an adult film star, and to prevent damage to his campaign.” Cohen later testified to a Manhattan court in 2024 that he submitted fake invoices for legal services in 2016 to cover up what were, in fact, reimbursements for $130,000 hush-money payments to Daniels and that that he knew the payment violated federal election law. After recording his chat with Trump, Cohen admitted to CNN that he had submitted a formal request for a pardon for the crimes he admitted to in 2018. Cohen said that he first submitted a pardon request during the presidency of Joe Biden, which was supported by a leading Democratic congressman, but not acted on. Recently, Cohen said, he changed the cover letter on the application to urge Trump to grant him clemency. One week after Donald Trump ordered his navy secretary to redesign a new aircraft carrier, the USS Doris Miller - to scrap the modern electromagnetic system used to launch fighter jets, and install old-fashioned steam-powered catapults instead - CNN reports that the navy is considering another change to the same ship: removing the name of Miller, a Black sailor known for his heroism during the 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor, and naming it instead the USS Donald Trump. The language of Trump’s executive order last week, demanding the change back to steam catapults, perhaps offered a hint that the name chosen during his first term, to honor Doris “Dorie” Miller, might be changed. The order did not refer to the ship at any point as the Miller, instead using just its hull number, CVN-81. A 21-year-old recent college graduate was behind an anonymous website that put out widely shared fake election polling in Wisconsin, Nevada and California, the Guardian can reveal. The website, Median Strategies, abruptly shut down and withdrew its polling earlier this week following questions from a reporter from the Los Angeles Times. In an unsigned statement, it described a “short-term social experiment” to examine how fake polling “could enter and spread through the political information ecosystem without independent verification”. “I wanted to see if fake polls could really penetrate the ecosystem that easily,” Rahil Prakash told the Guardian on Thursday when reached by phone. “And as it turned out, it could.” Karen Bass, the mayor of Los Angeles, touted Median polling data after it appeared to put her ahead of her election challenger by more than 10 percentage points. The poll was also cited by the California Post. A widely followed polling aggregator on X also shared the group’s Nevada poll, although several credible polling organizations did not aggregate Median polling because they could not verify its methodology. “Did I expect it to perhaps expedite in the way it did? Most definitely not,” said Prakash. “I did not expect the California political press to pick it up on their own.” He added: “I’ll apologize straight out to the campaigns of Karen Bass, Nithya Raman and Francesca Hong for this.” Raman is running against Bass in November’s LA mayoral election. Hong lost the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor earlier this month, after Median suggested she had led the race by more than 20 percentage points. It also released a fake poll showing the Nevada governor, Joe Lombardo, up by five points before November’s general election. chineseSummary: 尽管此前曾将特朗普比作“流氓”，但特朗普的前私人律师对他赞不绝口
chineseContent: 唐纳德·特朗普的前掮客兼私人律师迈克尔·科恩(Michael Cohen)在2019年对总统发起了攻击，当时他在国会作证时将特朗普比作暴徒。周四，他又进行了180度大转变，在科恩的纽约广播节目中播出的两人之间的友好对话中，他对总统大加赞扬。科恩在后台播放了 1970 年代 R&B 热门歌曲《Reunited》，并告诉听众周日收听更多采访内容，他在介绍这次谈话时表示，两人已经原谅了对方。科恩随后批评了那些认为“坚持仇恨是力量的标志”的人。众所周知，特朗普几十年来一直怀恨在心。在周四播出的谈话部分中，科恩完全支持特朗普毫无根据的说法，即如果他没有在 2024 年当选总统，伊朗现在就会获得核武器并摧毁以色列。这一说法与特朗普下令打击伊朗核浓缩设施前不久发布的 2025 年美国情报评估相矛盾，该评估称伊朗已于 2003 年放弃了对核武器的追求。在聊天中，科恩还试图将特朗普对他以前角色的记忆归咎于他的观点。最亲近的助手说：“老板，你还记得我在你身边的时候吗？”在谈话的另一个阶段，特朗普似乎默认了他实际上输掉了 2020 年总统选举，他告诉科恩：“我在边境当选——顺便说一句，这发生了两次”，然后提到了 2016 年和 2024 年的选举。特朗普接着声称，曼哈顿和纽约州检察官不公平地威胁科恩入狱，他们利用科恩的证词判定特朗普犯有竞选财务违规和欺诈罪。 2018年，科恩在联邦法院认罪或
